function_definition: Points to or identifies an entity, event, topic, or element of the discourse context.
Addresses the audience or calls on someone to act, respond, or pay attention.
Comments on the language, framing, or tone of the message itself.
Expresses the commenter's emotion, attitude, or evaluation.
Establishes, maintains, or closes social contact.
Enacts or reinforces a speech act, such as making a claim, commitment, or acknowledgement.
Contributes aesthetic, playful, ornamental, or wordplay effects.
Signals or contests identity, affiliation, belonging, exclusion, or political group positioning.
Performs a recognizable conversational or pragmatic function.
Organizes the visual structure or layout of the message.
Relates structurally to the verbal text by anchoring, complementing, modifying, repeating, or replacing it.
The emoji directly addresses or calls out the audience, a specific person, or a group.
The emoji instructs, commands, or urges the audience to take a specific action. It accompanies or substitutes for an imperative.
The emoji expresses a judgemental evaluation—contempt, ridicule, disapproval, or dismissal—towards a person, party, or political event. The stance is evaluative and directed at a target.
The emoji expresses a positive evaluation—admiration, approval, or appreciation—towards a person, action, or outcome.
The emoji expresses a negative emotional state in the commenter—sadness, fear, anger, frustration, or disgust—without necessarily targeting a specific person.
The emoji expresses the commenter's positive emotional state, such as joy, excitement, relief, or pride.
The emoji expresses a neutral or ambiguous emotional state, or accompanies a factual statement without clear positive or negative valence.
The emoji signals how the surrounding text should be interpreted, for example as ironic, hypothetical, or quoted. It provides an interpretive frame for the verbal content.
The emoji comments on or marks a specific language, dialect, or code being used in the message, or signals a code-switch.
The emoji explicitly labels the tone of the textual message, such as humorous, serious, sarcastic, angry, or gentle.

The emoji accompanies or reinforces expressions of the commenter's belief and their intention or desire that the hearer have or form a like belief. Covers assertions, claims, statements of fact, and declarations.
The emoji accompanies or reinforces expressions of the commenter's intention and belief that their utterance obligates them to do something—a commitment, promise, or pledge.

The emoji accompanies expressions of the commenter's feeling toward the hearer, or the commenter's intention that their utterance satisfy a social expectation to express certain feelings, and their belief that it does.
The emoji attracts the attention of other users, the original commenter, or a specific person in the thread, without a clear directive or appellative function.
The emoji marks the opening or end of a conversational exchange or comment thread, signalling the commenter's entry into the discussion, closure, or farewell.
The emoji signals the commenter's presence and engagement in the conversation without contributing specific content.
The emoji intentionally contributes aesthetic value to the crafted quality of the message.
The emoji creates general warmth or positive social rapport with the audience without primarily expressing the commenter's own emotion.
Emojis are repeated or sequenced to create visual rhythm, intensity, or emphasis through pattern, or meaning emerges from their combination rather than from any one emoji alone.

The emoji creates a visual or linguistic pun with the verbal text through formal similarities, such as sound, lexical, morphological, or semantic similarity. The motivation is playful linguistic creativity rather than social avoidance.
The emoji points to a specific entity or event in the immediate context of the comment or political situation, equivalent to 'this', 'here', or 'that one'.
The emoji introduces, labels, or marks the topic of the comment. It signals what the comment is about and may categorize or frame the subject matter.
The emoji signals the exclusion, othering, or rejection of a person or group, marking them as outside the in-group or as an enemy.
The emoji signals the commenter's diaspora identity—their location outside the country being discussed—while claiming connection to or investment in that country's political situation.
The emoji signals national identity, pride, or belonging to a national group, typically through flag emojis or national symbols.
The emoji signals identity affiliation, but the specific group or identity category cannot be determined from the comment context alone.

The emoji signals affiliation with or opposition to a specific political ideology, party, or political figure. This includes party-colour emojis, party-associated symbols, and emojis used as political badges.
The emoji rallies, energises, or mobilises members of a political group, urging collective action or reinforcing group solidarity in an activist sense.
The emoji ridicules, mocks, or belittles a political figure, party, or position, performing social dominance through humour or contempt.
The emoji expresses solidarity with or belonging to a political group, cause, or community, emphasizing in-group cohesion and shared identity.
The emoji accompanies or depicts a physical action being performed or described in the comment.
The emoji signals agreement with, endorsement of, or approval of the preceding statement, comment, or position.
The emoji indicates that the commenter is engaged, listening, or following along without adding new content.
The emoji resolves a specific ambiguity in verbal content that has multiple possible interpretations, clarifying meaning, tone, or register.
The emoji signals disagreement with, criticism of, or opposition to the preceding statement, comment, or position.
The emoji serves only as visual decoration and performs no further identifiable communicative function.

The emoji substitutes for a taboo, sensitive, or explicit referent through deliberate indirection motivated by social avoidance. It is distinct from poetic wordplay, which is motivated by formal or linguistic creativity.
The emoji is a graphic illustration of a word or expression in the comment.
The emoji specifically softens a potentially face-threatening message or adds courtesy to that message.
The comment or reply responds to a post or another commenter and consists only of one or more emoji.
The emoji humorously elaborates on, plays on, or parodies an idea introduced earlier in the comment thread.
A series of consecutive emojis conveys a narrative, rather than a single composite message.
The emoji changes the sentiment value, polarity, or intensity of the textual utterance without explicitly labelling its tone.
The emoji helps organize interaction by signalling entry into an exchange, responding to a prior comment, or passing the conversational floor to another commenter.
The emoji performs a social or pragmatic function not captured by the coding scheme. Use sparingly and record a private note.
The emoji occurs in a position or role normally occupied by a punctuation mark.
The emoji divides a comment into distinct sections, functioning like a heading or bullet-point separator.
The emoji signals that a summary or conclusion precedes or follows.
The emoji signals a shift from one topic, point, or segment to another within the same comment.
The emoji grounds or anchors the message by providing a concrete referential focal point for the verbal content.
The emoji adds meaning that complements but does not duplicate the verbal content, supplying information not present in the text.
The emoji modifies, intensifies, or highlights an adjacent word, phrase, or idea by changing its degree or quality or drawing attention to it.
The emoji repeats or duplicates meaning already conveyed by the verbal text, adding no new information but reinforcing the message.
The emoji directly replaces a word, phrase, or sentence; the verbal construction would otherwise be incomplete or ungrammatical.
